title: King safety
intro: Back-rank mates and careless king moves lose more games than any opening. Learn to spot the danger in time.

lessons.title: The back-rank mate
lessons.summary: A king walled in by its own pawns.

steps.text: The black king is shut in by its own pawns on f7, g7 and h7. If a rook or queen reaches the back row with check, it is mate.
Punish the weak back rank: checkmate in one.
steps.hint: The e-file is open to the back row.
steps.ifWrong: Not mate. Reach the back row with check.

steps.text: Your own king has the same problem! Black's rook threatens Rd1 mate. The cure is 'luft': a pawn move that gives your king an escape square, or a piece that guards your back row.
Black threatens Rd1 mate. Stop it.
steps.hint: Give your king an escape square, or guard the first row with your rook.
steps.ifWrong: After that, Rd1 is still mate. Make luft or guard the back row.

lessons.title: Block checks the smart way
lessons.summary: Answer a check with a developing move, and keep the right to castle.

steps.text: Black's bishop checks your king. You can move the king, take the checking piece, or block. Moving the king here costs you the right to castle.
Block the check with a move that also develops or helps your position.
steps.hint: Put a bishop, knight or pawn between the bishop and your king.
steps.ifWrong: Block the check, and keep your king where it can still castle.
steps.ifRight: Check blocked, a piece developed, and you can still castle.

feedback.e1e2: That escapes the check, but your king loses the right to castle and blocks your bishop.
feedback.d1d2: Blocking with the queen works, but she can be chased around. Use a bishop, knight or pawn.
